function.name: plant_biomass
function.description: Calculate the biomass of a plant species in a given area. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

species_name.description: The name of the plant species.

area.description: The area of the forest in square kilometers. This is a float type value.

density.description: The density of the plant species in the area. Default is average global density. This is a float type value.

I don’t have live access to real‑time weather or pollution feeds, so I can’t give you the exact AQI (Air Quality Index) reading at this moment. However: | What you’re looking for | Where to find it | |------------------------|------------------| | **Real‑time AQI** – values from 0–500 with categories such as “Good,” “Moderate,” etc. | • [AirNow](https://www.airnow.gov/)
• EPA’s *AirData* portal
• City/County dashboards (e.g., City of Los Angeles Environmental Services) | | **Historical trends & forecasts** | • NOAA Climate Prediction Center
• Local news sites often embed short‑term forecast widgets | | **Mobile alerts** | • Apps like Plume Labs’ Air Report, BreezoMeter, or EPA’s own app | If you want a quick snapshot, just search “Los Angeles AQI” on Google—Google pulls its own estimate from official sources and displays it directly under the query box. Feel free to let me know if you'd like help interpreting those numbers or setting up automated checks!
message.reasoning: The user asks about current air quality in LA. We don't have real-time data; we can provide general info and suggest checking an API or website like AirNow. No tool needed.
